reasoning: Programmatic-only: 1 major concern(s): Heading hierarchy broken

concerns.analysis: The heading hierarchy incorrectly reverses the containment relationship of major sections and their subsections. In the source PDF, 'SECTION 2' is a top-level heading, and 'Portable/Laptop Model and Options Pricing' is its subsection. However, in the JSON output, 'SECTION 2' is assigned Level 2, while its subsection 'Portable/Laptop Model and Options Pricing' is assigned Level 1, placing the subsection above its parent section in the hierarchy.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: SECTION 2: PC Volume Purchase Master Award 501326 Pricing (Parent section) ... Portable/Laptop Model and Options Pricing (Subsection)
concerns.output_quote: {"type": "heading", "level": 2, "text": "SECTION 2: PC Volume Purchase Master Award 501326 Pricing"} ... {"type": "heading", "level": 1, "text": "Portable/Laptop Model and Options Pricing"}

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 17 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=17, examples=['mailto:beverly.satterfield@nc.gov', 'mailto:beverly.satterfield@nc.gov', 'mailto:David.Cramb@dell.com']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

concerns.description: Table cells contain 21 unlinked URL(s)/email(s) that should be hyperlinks
concerns.analysis: bare_urls_in_tables=21. Examples: p2: [David.Cramb@dell.com](mailto:David.Cramb@dell.com; p2: David.Cramb@dell.com; p2: David.Cramb@dell.com. URLs and emails in table cells should be clickable links.

concerns.description: List numbering restart(s): 1 ordered list(s) restart numbering at 1 instead of continuing sequence
concerns.analysis: restart_count=1. Examples: p3: 2 single-item ordered lists (fragmented). Ordered lists that restart numbering suggest content was split across page breaks and not reassembled.

The source document uses underlining to provide visual emphasis (e.g., on words like 'no longer' and 'must' on page 2). In the output JSON, these words are formatted with markdown bold text (**no longer**, **must**) but the underline styling itself is completely lost. Since underline formatting requires explicit HTML tags (like <u>) when no markdown equivalent exists, this constitutes a loss of visual emphasis.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Requisitions no longer need to be sent... Award must be sent...
concerns.output_quote: **Please note:** Requisitions **no longer** need to be sent... Award **must** be sent...

concerns.analysis: flattened_sublists=18. Examples: p44 table: • HDMI® supports up to 4096x2160@60Hz, • USB-C® supports up to 5120x2880@60Hz; p46 table: • HDMI® supports up to 4096x2160@60Hz, • USB-C® supports up to 5120x2880@60Hz; p48 table: • HDMI® supports up to 4096x2160@60Hz, • USB-C® supports up to 5120x2880@60Hz.
